requirement:
Awaiting the builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. The harness obtains the submitted value under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission` has two clauses. The first says awaiting the builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting under `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. The second says the harness obtains the submitted value under `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. Both describe observable behavior: what the await yields and where the value comes from. Neither names a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or required delegation interface.

I considered one possible structural reading, that the builder must be awaitable and yield `R`. An implementation could produce the same `R` through a different mechanism, such as a different future type or a differently shaped builder. That would still satisfy the text, so the mechanism is discretionary.

The two cited requirements only supply context. The text cites them (`{cite}`) and does not delegate any structure to them. Any structural obligations they carry belong to their own assessments. No implementation roots are supplied and none are needed.

behavioral: The subject has one behavioral obligation. Awaiting the `Ask` builder returns the decoded `R` that passed answer vetting. How the harness obtains the submission and how vetting works belong to the cited requirements `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance` and `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. They are context only, so I did not reassess their tests.

The reviewed tests cover the obligation:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` submits `{"result":true}`. It asserts that awaiting `ask::<bool>()` returns `true`, so a scalar is decoded and returned.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[typed_submission_references_resolve]` submits a structured `{"result":{"decision":"Yes"}}`. It asserts that the awaited value decodes to an `Answer` with `Decision::Yes`, so a structured type is decoded and returned.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_collects_corrections_and_rechecks_every_callback]` submits `false` first and then `true`, with callbacks that request corrections. It asserts that the awaited result is `true`, the second submission that passed vetting. Not the first, rejected one. It also asserts that `seen == [false, true]`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_preserves_domain_errors_and_skips_later_callbacks]` covers the vetting failure path. Awaiting returns `Err(ValidationError::Graph(..))` and no value.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[ending_without_a_corrected_submission_is_an_agent_error]` show that no value is returned without an accepted submission.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[unknown_tools_return_errors_without_creating_inputs_or_preventing_submission]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[explicit_insertions_preserve_order_repetition_and_selection_snapshots]` also show a submitted value being decoded and returned (`true` and `answer.n == 7`).

All of these tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no uncovered obligation.

text: :::{req} judge.submission
Awaiting the builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. The harness obtains the submitted value under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`.
:::{req} vet_answer
Each call to `Ask::vet_answer` appends an independent `FnMut` callback to this
request in either builder phase.
For each decoded submission, the harness invokes the callbacks in registration
order with the same `&R`, stopping at the first `Err`. Each callback retains
its state across submissions in the same conversation.
If any callback returns `Err(error)`, the harness MUST stop running callbacks
and end the conversation immediately, even if an earlier callback requested a
correction. Awaiting the `Ask` MUST return
`Err(ValidationError::Graph(error))` carrying the original `D::Error`.
:::{req} submission.acceptance
The harness checks the submission count in a complete model response before
checking submission arguments. An otherwise valid submission while any search
page is open returns a tool error listing every outstanding `search_id` and
instructing the agent to call `finish_search` before resubmitting. The request
stays open and retains its submission reminder. Once all delivered searches
are accounted for under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior`,
exactly one `submit_result` call whose arguments are an object containing only
the `result` field supplies that field's value for decoding and vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. Acceptance ends the
conversation. Other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped.
Assistant prose remains conversation text.
